findings.title: Lethal Trifecta satisfied
findings.detail: Simon Willison's / Palo Alto Networks' framing: a skill is especially dangerous when it simultaneously has access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to communicate externally. airlock observed all legs in one run, which means this skill can be turned into an exfiltration channel by anything it reads -- including a web page or an email it was asked to summarise.

findings.title: Read ~/.git-credentials without declaring it
findings.detail: Access time advanced on a planted credential the skill never asked for. Read detection uses atime, which is a heuristic: it proves access but not intent, which is why the canary correlation above is what confirms exfiltration.

findings.title: Contacted 1 undeclared host(s)
findings.detail: The skill reached network destinations absent from its manifest. Under the OWASP Universal Skill Format, network permission is a domain allowlist rather than a boolean, precisely so this stays checkable.

findings.title: Declared but never used: /output/
findings.detail: Over-broad permission requests are the norm here -- Snyk found 280+ skills leaking credentials through over-permission alone. A permission the skill never exercises is one you can safely remove.
